**Checking sign-in on load**

`src/lib/auth.tsx` sets up auth with `configureAuth` from `react-query-auth`. Its `userFn` is `getUser`, which calls `GET /auth/me`. The session cookie is sent because the request interceptor in `src/lib/api-client.ts` sets `withCredentials = true`. `src/app/provider.tsx` wraps the whole app in `AuthLoader` (inside `QueryClientProvider`). On load, `AuthLoader` runs the `/auth/me` query and shows a spinner until it settles. Only then does it render the children. After that, `useUser()` returns the cached result everywhere. `ProtectedRoute` in `auth.tsx`, used in `src/app/router.tsx`, checks `useUser().data`. If there is no user, it does a `<Navigate replace>` to the login page, passing the current pathname as `redirectTo`.

**Handling a 401**

The response interceptor in `src/lib/api-client.ts` handles every API error, including the `/auth/me` call. It first reads `error.response.data.message`, falling back to `error.message`. It shows that text as an error toast through `useNotifications`. If the status is 401, it then sets `window.location.href` to the login path from `paths.auth.login.getHref(redirectTo)`. This is a full page navigation, not a router navigation. Finally it rejects the promise, so callers still see the error.

**Gotcha in the 401 redirect**

The `redirectTo` logic looks buggy. It builds a new empty `URLSearchParams()` and reads `redirectTo` from that. The lookup always returns null, so the value always falls back to `window.location.pathname`. That happens to work for the "come back to where I was" case. The `searchParams.get` call is dead code, though. Also, an unauthenticated visitor's `/auth/me` returns 401, so they get an error toast and a hard redirect to login even on first load.
